page: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-intel is a High Performance virtual machine configured with 12 vCPUs and 24.0 GB of system memory. The underlying hardware features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, structured as 6 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is shared, which introduces potential resource contention tradeoffs. Local storage is bundled with a 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results position this server in the average tier across most standard compute and memory tests. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1418.58 and a multi-core score of 17309.27. Memory performance shows a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1224.9 GB/sec, which drops to 87.74 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 47.62 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the server demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 11.99 GB/sec and processed 18.53 million Redis SET operations per second.

The server exhibits limitations in demanding machine learning tasks. While LLM inference for a small 135M model reaches 719.57 tokens/sec for prompt processing, performance drops to a weak rating of 16.55 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and shared CPU allocation, this configuration offers a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring moderate parallel processing and fast local storage without sustained peak CPU demands. Suitable workloads include software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and general-purpose application hosting.
description: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-intel is a High Performance virtual server featuring 12 vCPUs and 24.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 6 physical cores with hyper-threading, a shared CPU allocation model, and a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD. Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard compute and memory metrics, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8081.0 and a static web serving throughput of 11.99 GB/sec. However, resource tradeoffs are evident in complex tasks, as shown by weak performance in medium-sized LLM inference. This server represents a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that benefit from a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and fast local storage, such as software compilation, database operations, and web serving, provided they do not require dedicated CPU cores.
